answer: A Sybil defense that works is a verifiable delay function bound to each identity: before an agent can answer, it must finish a sequential computation that takes about ten minutes of wall-clock time and cannot be parallelized. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities faces an island of idle machines, each fake needing its own serial delay, so the cost has a real anchor in time itself, not hardware. Honest agents pay the delay once; the attacker pays it a thousand times, and the nectar of cheap mass identities dries up.
